Thanks for the intro — a few items from our side to make the handoff smoother. Attached is a short spec with sample prompts/response pairs and our current traffic profile (Lumen_Onboarding_Specs.pdf). High-level asks: 

- Model shortlist: we need a recommendation set that balances cost and medical-domain accuracy for clinical note summarization and triage assistance.
- Context: many of our notes are long (average 1,600 tokens, 95th percentile ~4,500). We need advice on whether to use 8k context, sliding window, or on-the-fly retrieval to keep cost/p95 latency in check.
- Volume: initial pilot ~30k unique users/month, expected 12k daily active; average 2 calls/user/day during trial. Peak concurrency estimate: 250 qps during manual triage windows.
- Quality SLOs: top-tier summaries should exceed our current heuristic F1 baselines; latency p95 target <= 1.5s for single-shot summarization where possible.

Next steps we want from Redwood: model shortlist with quantized variants, token footprint estimate (tokens/day, tokens/month), recommended context strategy, and a short mutual action plan for a 2-week sprint. Also happy to provide sample de-identified notes if that helps.

Thanks,
Sara Lambert
Director, Clinical AI
Lumen Health

Sara — thanks for the spec, that was very helpful. High-level reply below and a proposed MiA (mutual action) plan attached (MAF_v1.docx). Summary:

1) Model shortlist (recommended for pilot)
   - rwd-alpha-13B-instruct (8k) — strong out-of-the-box summarization, good latency/cost balance on A100-style GPUs; recommend 4-bit quant for pilot.
   - mistral-instruct-7B-8k — lighter compute, competitive for instruction-following tasks; use as fallback for cost-sensitive paths.
   - elk-lite-3B-ctx16k (retrieval-first) — for longer-context workflows where we push heavy retrieval and chunking; good for recall-sensitive triage.

2) Context strategy
   - Default: 8k context on rwd-alpha for full-note summarization where we can fit content. For notes >8k tokens, use a retrieval + chunk-ranking flow and then a final aggregation prompt (we call this the "prefix+stitch" pattern).
   - For p95 latency-sensitive endpoints (quick triage), use distilled-run on mistral-instruct with a 2–3 chunk context (fast path) and fallback to rwd-alpha if quality check triggers.

3) Token footprint (pilot sizing) — rough estimates based on your volumes and sample set:
   - Active users/day: 12,000; calls/user/day: 2 => ~24k calls/day.
   - Avg tokens/request (prompt + expected completion): 2,500 tokens (mix of long notes + prompts).
   - Tokens/day: ~60M tokens/day, Tokens/month (30d): ~1.8B tokens.
   - Peak concurrency 250 qps would transiently raise per-second token throughput—recommend burst capacity on Dedicated or Hosted with autoscale.

4) Compute guidance & batching
   - Pilot: 2 x A100-40GB (or single H100 80GB equivalent) + scaled pool of 4 x 80GB for heavy bursts; use continuous batching with max_batch_latency=15ms to balance latency.
   - KV cache for multi-step dialogs is useful but for single-shot summarization we'll rely on request-level batching and prefix cache to offload repeated templates.

5) Data/security and docs
   - We'll attach SOC2 summary and a copy of our onboarding playbook in the next note. For procurement, if you loop in procurement@lumenhealth.com we can push templates.

6) Mutual Action Plan (2 week pilot kickoff)
   - Day 0–2: contract/procurement alignment, SOC2 & data transfer agreement sign-off.
   - Day 3–7: infra provisioning, sample dataset ingestion, initial traffic replay for load estimates.
   - Day 8–12: model tuning/temperature sweeps, latency tuning (batch size, concurrency), basic evals vs baseline.
   - Day 13–14: pilot handoff, success criteria review, go/no-go for expansion.

Action items for you: share one de-identified batch (5–10 notes) and confirm whether we should enable encryption-at-rest keying with your KMS. We'll also prepare a token-profile CSV (attached) with per-endpoint estimates so your finance team can model cost.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync to walk through the shortlist and run a quick Q&A.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Confirming those math checks out. A couple of ops-specifics to add: 
- Token mix variance: assume a 20% heavy tail where ~5% of requests hit >6k tokens; plan for preemptive chunking on those records.
- Suggested Dedicated pool for pilot: 6x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs with burst autoscale to +50% during peak windows. That keeps p95 latency headroom and lets us run validation re-runs without affecting live traffic.
- Suggested batching: target batch sizes 4–8 for rwd-alpha-13B with a max latency budget of 250ms for single-shot summarization endpoints. For mistral-instruct fallbacks use batch 16 if latency SLAs allow.

I'll schedule an infra scoping call with our infra ops on Wed to pin exact GPU counts and network egress estimates (important for cost model).

—Ben
